create.name: Samadhi Buddhist Vihara
create.bio:
Samadhi Buddhist Vihara is a Theravada Buddhist temple at Rolleston, just south-west of Christchurch in Canterbury, New Zealand. It opened in May 2002 under the guidance of Venerable Makuldeniye Somarathana Thero, known as Bhante Soma, who was ordained in Sri Lanka at twelve and remains its chief incumbent. It is the main Sri Lankan Buddhist temple in the South Island and also serves Buddhists in Dunedin and Invercargill, with a trust drawn from both cities that looks after the property.

The temple's resident monks lead meditation twice a week: an English-language session on Sunday evenings and a Sinhala-language session on Wednesdays, both with Venerable Mapalane Sumanatissa Thero, who also takes meditation questions on weekday evenings. Through the year there are full-moon observance days, Dhamma discussions during the rains retreat, meditation retreats and festivals such as Vesak and the Kathina robe offering, many of them recorded on the temple's YouTube channel. A Dhamma library and a weekly Sri Lankan language and culture school for children complete its work.

free_resources.title: Meditation sessions
free_resources.description: Weekly insight meditation at the temple with Venerable Mapalane Sumanatissa Thero: an English-language evening on Sundays and a Sinhala-language evening on Wednesdays, with time on weekday evenings for questions about practice.

free_resources.title: All Night Pirith Chanting & Kathina Robe Offering Ceremony 2026
free_resources.description: The temple's annual end-of-rains festival: a night of protective chanting from the evening of 20 November into the next morning, followed on 22 November by the offering of the Kathina robe to the monks.
